content.comment_body: Hello everyone. Can the value of an On delay timer be set using a basic operator panel connected to a [product_name]? I’m asking because my [product_name] version doesn’t have its own panel, so I can’t adjust settings directly.

Yes, that’s possible. You need to create a VM value in [product_name]. Check the attached example. In [product_name] engineering software, go to TOOLS → Parameter VM Mapping. The first line sets the timer value (currently 6), and the second line is the time base (currently seconds); this usually remains unchanged. You can adjust this value on your HMI screen. Alternatively, you could use a [product_name] operator device.
Thank you! That was extremely helpful!
Hello, [user_name]. Could you resend your program for timers in [product_name]? I’m encountering an error when opening the file.
To open this file, you need at least version 8.1 of the [product_name] engineering software.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are troubleshooting how to modify timer settings on a [product_name] device without onboard controls, using a basic operator panel. It’s confirmed that timer values are adjustable via mapped variables seen from the HMI. Discussion also touches on compatibility issues when opening shared project files with outdated engineering software versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want to adjust timer settings on a [product_name] device using the HMI, even when the hardware lacks built-in adjustment options.
